curvature_limit.relief_source: Measured 2026-11-17 on MOLA MEGDR radius (megr) grids, radius - 3 396 000 m: 16 ppd max +21 280 m (Olympus Mons, 17.34 N 226.97 E), min -23 170 m (76.97 N: the oblate figure, not a basin); 4 ppd +21 241 / -22 931 m. Bounds +21.5 / -23.4 km include margin (science/worlds/tests/test_mars.py).
curvature_limit.note: Bins below beyond_range_world_bound_elev_deg could still be raised by terrain <= H_world_max_m beyond max_range_m (world-wide bound; a conservative flag, not a detected obstruction).

method.visible_pct: share of hourly Horizons samples (both endpoints included) with the body centre above the skyline (perpendicular margin > 0); NO bisection refinement (any-site default)
method.longest_hidden_h: longest run of consecutive hidden hourly samples x step_h
method.disk_mean: trapezoid over hourly samples of the visible-disk fraction
method.unknown: samples over no-data skyline bins count as hidden

metrics.disclaimer: Local geometric visibility only: not certified illumination, power, or DSN link availability.
metrics.window_label: one Mars year (687 d) of hourly samples

sources.description: JPL Horizons observer tables CENTER=coord@499 (CYLINDRICAL site), QUANTITIES=4,13,20, APPARENT=AIRLESS

limitations: Local geometric terrain visibility only; not certified illumination/power or DSN telecom availability.
Single ray per 0.5 deg azimuth bin at the bin centre; sub-bin peaks can be missed.
Hourly samples, no bisection refinement of crossings.
Horizons az/el (ellipsoid normal) rotated to the sphere normal used by the skyline.
Product members are alternative terrain products, not calibrated probabilities.
Requirements copied from the Moon team as ENGINEERING ASSUMPTIONS unless the world states its own.
Atmosphere: Horizons APPARENT=AIRLESS (no refraction; see world.atmosphere_note for the estimate).
Mars atmosphere: no refraction (estimated ~0.007 deg at the horizon), no sky model; energy = direct beam only for explicit tau values (ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION).
Relay orbiters (MRO, MAVEN, TGO, Mars Express): not available for this world (no ephemerides wired); comms = direct-to-Earth geometry and the SEP rule only.
CTX DEM heights are areoid heights (tested), converted with the MOLA 16 ppd areoid.
The site is a rule-selected rim high point, not a surveyed landing site.

world.name: mars
world.shape: sphere R = 3 396 000 m for heights and rays (MOLA MEGDR reference radius). Horizons uses the IAU ellipsoid 3396.19/3396.19/3376.20 km; the site is passed in cylindrical coordinates so its radius is exact. Mars is oblate (f = 0.0059): geodetic - planetocentric latitude ~0.24 deg at 18 N, handled by the az/el frame tie.
world.body_fixed_frame: Horizons: IAU_MARS (west-positive; converted to east-positive), IAU 2015 model. DEMs: MOLA MEGDR IAU 2000 planetocentric east-positive; longitude tie applied (frame_tie)
world.spice_kernels: not loaded; NAIF text PCKs pck00010/pck00011 read by science/worlds/pck.py for the tie only

rotation.periodic_terms: plus periodic terms (largest 0.419 deg in alpha0, 1.591 deg in delta0, 0.585 deg in W, period ~7e5 yr) evaluated from NAIF pck00011 by science/worlds/pck.py for the frame tie

world.relief_source: Measured 2026-11-17 on MOLA MEGDR radius (megr) grids, radius - 3 396 000 m: 16 ppd max +21 280 m (Olympus Mons, 17.34 N 226.97 E), min -23 170 m (76.97 N: the oblate figure, not a basin); 4 ppd +21 241 / -22 931 m. Bounds +21.5 / -23.4 km include margin (science/worlds/tests/test_mars.py).

B (30 Sep 2010), section 2.3: standard downlink BPSK link design and coding achieve X-band data return at SEP angles down to at least 2.3 deg, and Ka-band down to 1 deg. https://deepspace.jpl.nasa.gov/dsndocs/810-005/106/106B.pdf

conjunctions.note: Outage = superior conjunction with SEP below the X-band threshold (coronal scintillation, module 106). Inferior conjunctions below the threshold put the Sun near the ground antenna beam (noise, module 105): flagged, not assessed, not counted as outage.

comms.threshold_source: DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook 810-005, module 106 "Solar Corona and Solar Wind Effects", Rev. B (30 Sep 2010), section 2.3: standard downlink BPSK link design and coding achieve X-band data return at SEP angles down to at least 2.3 deg, and Ka-band down to 1 deg. https://deepspace.jpl.nasa.gov/dsndocs/810-005/106/106B.pdf

frame_tie.dem_frame_source: MOLA MEGDR labels: "Map coordinates use the IAU2000 reference system" (Seidelmann et al. 2002: W0 176.630, Wdot 350.89198226, pole 317.68143/52.88650, unchanged in the IAU 2009 report = NAIF pck00010 BODY499). CTX DEMs are aligned to HRSC, itself tied to MOLA.

seasons_and_energy.label: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION (direct beam, Beer-Lambert, tau input; diffuse omitted)
seasons_and_energy.ls_source: Allison, M., McEwen, M. (2000), Planet. Space Sci. 48, 215-235 (Mars24 algorithm, NASA GISS)
seasons_and_energy.method:
Mars surface solar energy, direct beam only — ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION, tau an explicit input.

    S(r)      = S0 / r_AU^2,  S0 = 1361 W/m^2 (total solar irradiance at 1 AU; Kopp & Lean 2011, GRL 38, L01706)
    mu        = sin(e_sun)  (Sun-centre elevation above the sphere-normal horizon plane; Horizons, airless)
    G_dir,h   = S(r) mu exp(-tau / mu)  if the Sun centre is above the terrain skyline and mu >= MU_MIN, else 0
Beer-Lambert extinction with a plane-parallel air mass 1/mu (cut at mu < MU_MIN = 0.05, e < 2.9 deg, where 1/mu
diverges and the plane-parallel air mass is wrong). The DIFFUSE sky term is OMITTED: on Mars it is a large share of the
total at tau >~ 1 (Appelbaum & Flood 1990, Solar Energy 45, 353), so these numbers are the direct component only, a lower
bound on insolation, not a power prediction. No Mars sky-brightness MODEL is shipped. Daily energy = trapezoid of hourly
samples. Panel orientation, dust deposition on panels, temperature and conversion efficiency are not modelled.
seasons_and_energy.note: Energy is per unit horizontal area, direct beam only; diffuse sky light omitted (no sky MODEL shipped). Seasons split the hourly samples by Ls quarter; a season shorter than its full span at the window ends is labelled by its first/last UTC.

solar_day.method: mean interval between local noons (parabolic peak of hourly Sun elevation) over the window

ls_vs_horizons_subsolar_latitude.method: asin(sin 25.19 deg sin Ls(Allison & McEwen)) vs Horizons quantity 14 sub-solar latitude seen from the Sun centre (planetodetic -> planetocentric on the Horizons radii)

subsolar_independent_check.method: Sun direction recomputed from the sub-solar point (Sun-centred quantity 14, planetocentric latitude, W-longitude advanced by Wdot x Sun-Mars light time, frame tie removed) vs the topocentric table after the ellipsoid -> sphere tie

mola_data_density.note: MOLA MEGDR counts (megc); bins without shots are interpolated in the MEGDR.

sky_model.reason: no Mars sky-brightness / diffuse MODEL shipped; energy is direct beam only

threshold_source.label: ENGINEERING ASSUMPTION (no Mars mission requirement in this repo)
